critical_high.element: Matching-rules overlay — Close (×) button and click-outside-the-sheet (backdrop)
critical_high.finding: Closing the overlay via × or by clicking outside the sheet discards any unsaved matching-rule changes immediately, with no confirmation or discard prompt.
critical_high.user_impact: A user who has just set up or edited the matching rule and dismisses the overlay by the × (a very common 'I'm done' gesture) or an accidental outside click loses the entire configuration silently — the rule reverts to whatever was last saved with no indication anything was lost, so the user believes the task is complete when it is not.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Before discarding, compare the draft to the last saved rule and show a confirm/discard prompt (or an inline 'unsaved changes' warning) whenever the overlay is closed with a modified draft.

evidence.action: Reviewed closeOverlay() and its bindings: $('closeX').onclick = closeOverlay, and the backdrop click listener calls closeOverlay() when the click target is the backdrop itself; closeOverlay() only removes the 'open' class.
evidence.observed: No comparison between draft and saved state, no confirm dialog, and no 'unsaved changes' warning exists anywhere in the close path — the sheet just disappears and the in-progress draft is dropped, matching the state map's direct observation that closing with unsaved changes produced no discard prompt and the overlay closed immediately.

also.finding: Closing the overlay after changing a rule exits immediately with no "discard changes?" warning of any kind.

critical_high.element: "Then refine" section, first time "Use custom rules" is selected
critical_high.finding: Switching to "Use custom rules" auto-populates two already-enabled "Then refine" conditions (Invoice note contains…, Payment note contains…) that the user never added, even though the mode is described as narrowing first and then "optionally" refining.
critical_high.user_impact: A user assumes no extra narrowing is active, since the refine list looks like an ordinary empty-by-default builder, and saves a matching rule that is silently stricter than intended — invoices that should match the payment can fail to match.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Start "Then refine" empty on first-time custom setup and let the user add conditions explicitly, or visibly badge the two auto-seeded rows as suggested/unconfirmed defaults rather than rendering them identically to user-added ones.

evidence.action: Selected "Use custom rules" for the first time (per the recorded radio interaction) and traced the resulting state through seedCustomRows()/renderRows() in the prototype.
evidence.observed: Two removable condition rows render as enabled/active in "Then refine" and the "No extra conditions" empty-state text never appears, even though "+ Add condition" was never clicked.

also.finding: Switching to 'Use custom rules' for the first time auto-populates two refine conditions (Invoice note contains Memo on statement; Payment note contains Memo on statement) instead of starting empty.

evidence.quote: S1.1: on first open the engine is off, the default matching behaviour is displayed as NON-EDITABLE reference information, and no configuration is pre-filled.

critical_high.element: Settings configurator overlay (opened from 'Set up matching')
critical_high.finding: The page behind the overlay is not made inert while the overlay is open, so the overlay does not actually trap focus.
critical_high.user_impact: A keyboard user tabbing through the overlay can tab straight past its last control onto background page elements, losing the modal context and potentially acting on controls they can no longer see.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Mark the background inert (e.g. inert attribute or aria-hidden plus a focus trap) for as long as the overlay is open, per the standard dialog pattern.

evidence.action: opened the configurator and checked background reachability while it was open
evidence.observed: environment record: page behind the overlay inert while open = false

critical_high.element: Integration selector (Integration) sharing one matching-rule draft/saved state
critical_high.finding: The matching-rule configurator keeps a single saved/draft rule object that isn't keyed by the selected integration, so switching the Integration selector between two different integrations shows (and would save) the same rule set as belonging to whichever one is currently picked.
critical_high.user_impact: An accountant setting up a custom rule for one integration and then switching to review another integration on the same client (or a different client) could unknowingly carry that rule over and save it against the wrong integration, causing payments there to be matched to the wrong invoices.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Key the saved/draft matching-rule state by integration id and reload the correct rule set whenever the Integration selector changes.

evidence.source: vocabulary.md Organizational Terms — "Organization ... has accounting company + integrations + subscription plan": each integration is a distinct entity, so matching-rule configuration must not bleed across integrations.

critical_high.element: Custom rules panel — Customer scope row
critical_high.finding: Nowhere in the custom rules panel does a 'customer inheritance' setting appear, even though the Customer scope row's enable checkbox can be unchecked.
critical_high.user_impact: A user can disable the Customer scope with no way to configure how the payment's customer gets decided, leaving the core matching rule underspecified for that combination.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Add the customer-inheritance control (required, blocking save when off) and surface it whenever the Customer scope row is disabled.

evidence.quote: Customer inheritance ('a payment that matches an invoice takes its customer from that invoice') is available AND REQUIRED only when the Customer scope row is off. Saving with Customer off and inheritance off must be blocked.

critical_high.element: Integration select (#gspIntegration) vs. the 'Using defaults' / 'Custom rules' badge (#rulesStatus) and the saved matching rules it reflects
critical_high.claims: The badge and the rules opened via 'Configure matching rules' apply to whichever integration is currently selected in the Integration dropdown at the top of the Invoices panel.
critical_high.actual: The saved matching-rule state (`saved`) is a single global object that is never keyed by, or reset on, the selected integration; switching the Integration dropdown does not reload, clear, or re-scope it in any way.
critical_high.finding: Configuring custom matching rules while 'mzkt.by · Stripe' is selected, then switching the Integration dropdown to 'another-shop · Stripe', leaves the 'Custom rules' badge shown and the same custom rows in force for the new integration, with nothing on screen indicating the displayed rules were actually set up for a different integration.
critical_high.user_impact: The user believes they configured (or can verify) rules specific to the newly selected integration, and lets Synder apply payments to invoices using the previous integration's matching logic, risking payments applied to the wrong open invoice in the wrong set of books.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Key the matching-rule state (and the badge/Configure-link state) by the selected integration id, and reload the panel to that integration's own saved/default state whenever the Integration select changes.

evidence.action: Select 'mzkt.by · Stripe' → open matching rules → choose 'Use custom rules', keep the seeded scope rows → click Update (badge becomes 'Custom rules') → change the Integration select to 'another-shop · Stripe'.
evidence.observed: The 'Custom rules' badge remains displayed and 'Configure matching rules' still opens the exact custom rows configured under mzkt.by; no indicator, reset, or warning marks the rules as belonging to a different integration.

critical_high.element: 'Then refine' — per-row and/or dropdown (aria-label 'Combine refine conditions with and or or')
critical_high.finding: Every refine condition row renders its own AND/OR dropdown, which reads as an independent join for that pair of conditions, but all rows share a single underlying mode: changing any one dropdown snaps every other row's dropdown to the same value.
critical_high.user_impact: A user building 3+ refine conditions who intends mixed logic (e.g. A and B, or C) believes they've set that up because each row shows its own control, then saves a rule that silently applies the same join to everything — payments get matched to the wrong invoices with no error or warning anywhere in the flow.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Render a single shared and/or control for the whole refine list (not one per row), or implement true independent per-pair joins so the per-row control isn't misleading.

evidence.action: Inspected the refine join control: changed the and/or select on one refine row (value cycled and → or → and) with multiple refine conditions present, then traced setRefineMode() in the source.
evidence.observed: setRefineMode() writes draft.refineAny (one boolean) and then forces every '.nl-join-select' in the DOM to that same value — so all rows always display and enforce one shared mode, never independent per-row logic.

critical_high.element: Settings configurator overlay — Escape key
critical_high.finding: Pressing Escape while the overlay is open does not close it.
critical_high.user_impact: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user relying on the standard Escape-to-dismiss convention has no way to close the overlay except by tabbing to and activating the small × Close control.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Bind the Escape key to the same close/discard handler as the × Close button.

evidence.action: pressed Escape with the overlay open (focus at open was on the 'openRules' control)
evidence.observed: Escape closed the overlay: false

critical_high.element: Narrow the search — select with no accessible name
critical_high.finding: The select that chooses which field to match on (invoice number / payment note) exposes no accessible name.
critical_high.user_impact: A screen-reader user hears only the current combo-box value with no label for what it belongs to, so they can't tell what choice they're making without sight of the surrounding text.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Attach a visible label or aria-label describing the field, e.g. 'Match on field'.

evidence.action: inspected accessible name while changing value invoice_number → payment_note → invoice_number
evidence.observed: accessible name recorded as '(no accessible name) select'

also.finding: The checkbox that scopes/narrows the invoice search exposes no accessible name.

evidence.action: inspected accessible name while toggling checked state false → true → true
evidence.observed: accessible name recorded as '(no accessible name) input'

critical_high.element: "Key" field under Then refine (shown only after picking a metadata source) and the "Fix the highlighted fields" banner
critical_high.finding: Nothing marks the Key field as required when a metadata source is chosen; the user only learns it's mandatory after pressing Update and getting a generic "Fix the highlighted fields" banner with a small "Required" note buried in the row.
critical_high.user_impact: The user doesn't understand why saving failed or which of several fields is the problem, and is likely to give up on the custom setup rather than hunt for the highlighted field.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Label the Key field as required the moment a metadata source is picked (e.g. "Key (required)"), so the requirement is visible before submit, not only after a rejected save.

critical_high.element: "Configure matching rules →" link under "Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions"
critical_high.finding: Turning the "Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions" switch off greys out "Configure matching rules →" with nothing on screen explaining why it just stopped working.
critical_high.user_impact: The user assumes the button, or the page, is broken and may reload or leave rather than realizing they need to switch "Apply payments" back on first.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Add a short inline note next to the greyed-out link, e.g. "Turn on Apply payments above to edit matching rules."

critical_high.element: "Update" button on the Invoices settings page (gspUpdate) — confirmation toast
critical_high.finding: Saving the book-affecting Invoices toggles (Apply payments, Cancel sync, Sync unpaid invoices, Sync zero invoices) confirms with an internal codename instead of a real product term.
critical_high.user_impact: A bookkeeper working across many client integrations gets no indication from the confirmation of what was actually changed, undermining confidence that a book-affecting settings change really saved.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Replace the toast with a concrete confirmation naming the actual settings, e.g. "Invoice settings updated!", following the {Thing} {past participle}! pattern.

evidence.source: vocabulary.md Toast Patterns (Success: "{Thing} {past participle}!", e.g. "Settings updated!") — "GSP" is not in the UI Words canonical terms table and the toast is missing the required exclamation mark.

critical_high.element: "Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions" toggle vs. the overlay title "Apply payments to invoices in books"
critical_high.finding: The same rule is called "unpaid Invoice transactions" on the settings row (and its sub-copy "the matching unpaid Invoice transaction") but "invoices in books" one click away in the overlay it opens, mixing a synced transaction record with a ledger invoice for the same setting.
critical_high.user_impact: An accountant could believe the toggle governs which incoming platform transactions get synced rather than which invoice already posted in the books a payment is applied to, risking a misconfigured rule for the exact task this screen exists for.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Use one consistent term — "invoices in your books" — in both the settings-row label/description and the overlay title, reserving "transaction" for the payment/platform side.

evidence.quote: Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions
evidence.source: Domain scope: "Missing distinctions: flows that blur payment vs. invoice vs. transaction vs. payout"; vocabulary.md Books vs. Integration distinction (ledger inside the accounting company vs. the data source).

critical_high.element: Matching rules overlay — no 'Cancel sync' control
critical_high.finding: 'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment' exists only on the GSP Invoices page; the overlay never shows or lets the user change it, and the code explicitly avoids writing it from the overlay.
critical_high.user_impact: A user configuring matching rules inside the overlay has no visibility into or control over the cancel-on-no-match behaviour without leaving the overlay.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Surface the single stored cancel-sync value inside the overlay as well, editable from either surface.

evidence.quote: 'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment' is ONE stored value shown on both the overlay and GSP; either surface can change it and the other inherits. Not a second copy.

critical_high.element: Per-row 'Combine refine conditions with and or or' select, rendered once for every refine-condition row
critical_high.claims: Each refine condition's own and/or dropdown independently sets how that specific condition joins with the others, the same way the scope section shows one join marker per row.
critical_high.actual: Every refine-row dropdown is bound to the same single shared flag (draft.refineAny); changing any one row's dropdown immediately overwrites every other row's dropdown to the identical value.
critical_high.finding: With two or more refine conditions on screen, the UI shows multiple independent-looking join controls, but only one real join setting exists — changing one row silently rewrites the visible value of every sibling row with no explanation that they are linked.
critical_high.user_impact: A user trying to build a mixed rule (condition 1 with AND, condition 2 with OR) will unknowingly end up with the last-touched value applied to every condition, producing a broader- or narrower-matching rule than intended and changing which payments get auto-applied to which invoices.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Render the and/or control once (e.g. between conditions) instead of once per row, or visibly tie the dropdowns together so it is clear they always move as one.

evidence.action: Add two refine conditions → set the first row's join dropdown to 'or' → inspect the second row's join dropdown → set the second row's dropdown to 'and'.
evidence.observed: Setting the first dropdown to 'or' changes the second dropdown's displayed value to 'or' as well; setting the second back to 'and' changes the first back to 'and' too — there is no per-row precedence, only a single shared value presented as if it were per-row.

critical_high.element: 'Update' button in the GSP Invoices panel footer (#gspUpdate) and its toast/'Saved' hint
critical_high.claims: Clicking Update saves the panel's toggle settings (including 'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found') and the toast/hint confirms that save succeeded.
critical_high.actual: The click handler unconditionally fires the 'GSP settings updated' toast and the 'Saved' hint with no validation and no reference to any actual save outcome; there is no code path anywhere in the panel that can ever surface a failed save.
critical_high.finding: The success confirmation is shown every time regardless of whether the settings could actually be persisted, so 'Saved' carries no real information about whether state-changing toggles like the cancel-sync rule actually took effect.
critical_high.user_impact: If a real save ever failed, the user would still see 'Saved' / 'GSP settings updated' and trust that, e.g., cancel-sync-on-no-match is active, when it may not be — leading to payments posting without an invoice application when the user believed sync would instead be cancelled.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Gate the toast/hint on an actual save result and add a visible failure state (banner or error toast) for the case where the save does not succeed.

evidence.action: Toggle 'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment' on → click Update.
evidence.observed: The toast 'GSP settings updated' and the hint 'Saved' appear immediately and unconditionally; nothing in the UI can ever represent a failed save for this action.

critical_high.element: Metadata "Key" input and the "keep Customer or invoice-number on" scope requirement
critical_high.finding: Required-field state — a missing metadata Key, or a scope with neither Customer nor invoice-number matching enabled — is only revealed after the user clicks Update and the save fails; there is no indication while the field is being filled in.
critical_high.user_impact: A user who picks "Payment metadata" or "Invoice metadata" as a match source, or disables both scope conditions, gets no warning until the end of setup, discovers the problem only on a failed save, and must hunt for what to fix.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Surface the required-key and scope-requirement messaging as soon as the offending state occurs (e.g., on blur or immediately on selection), not only after a failed submit.

evidence.action: Set a scope row's source to "Payment metadata" without entering a key, then reviewed applyFieldErrors()/validation(), which only run their error-display path when submitAttempted is true.
evidence.observed: No red border or "Required" text appears while editing the Key field; both appear only after Update is clicked once and the save fails.

critical_high.element: "Update" button — one inside the matching-rules overlay (sheet-chrome), one on the Invoices panel footer (gsp-foot)
critical_high.finding: Two same-label, same-style primary "Update" buttons exist in the same flow, saving different, non-overlapping sets of settings — the overlay's Update never commits the page-level toggles, and the page's Update never touches the matching rule.
critical_high.user_impact: A user who toggles "Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found" and then opens, configures, and saves the matching-rules overlay sees a success toast ("Matching rules updated") and reasonably assumes everything is saved; the Cancel-sync change is silently lost until the separate outer Update is also clicked.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Give the two buttons distinct labels (e.g., "Save rules" inside the overlay) or have the overlay's save also commit any pending page-level toggle changes.

evidence.action: Toggled "Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found" on the Invoices panel, opened the matching-rules overlay, changed a rule, and clicked the overlay's Update (saveBtn).
evidence.observed: saveBtn's handler only clones draft into saved and closes the overlay with a toast; the Cancel-sync checkbox is committed solely by the separate #gspUpdate handler, which the user was never prompted to use.

critical_high.element: Per-row AND/OR select shown next to every "Then refine" condition row
critical_high.finding: Each refine condition row renders its own AND/OR dropdown, implying independent per-row logic, but changing any one of them instantly forces every other row's dropdown to the same value — there is effectively one shared setting rendered as many separate-looking controls.
critical_high.user_impact: A user trying to mix logic (e.g., treat one pair of conditions as AND and another as OR) changes one dropdown, sees all the others silently flip to match, and cannot tell why their other selection changed or reproduce the combination they wanted.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Show a single AND/OR control for the whole refine list (as the underlying model already is) instead of one per row, or implement true per-row/segment logic if mixed combinations are meant to be supported.

evidence.action: Added a second refine condition and inspected the join select's onchange handler (setRefineMode), which is wired to every ".nl-join-select" in the list.
evidence.observed: setRefineMode() sets draft.refineAny and then forces document.querySelectorAll('#refineRows .nl-join-select') to the same value, so all rows' dropdowns change together regardless of which one was edited.

critical_high.element: Overlay close (×) button and backdrop click-outside
critical_high.finding: Closing the matching-rules overlay via the × button or a click outside the sheet discards any in-progress edits immediately, with no 'unsaved changes' confirmation, regardless of how much of the rule was configured.
critical_high.user_impact: A user who has just finished narrowing scope, adding refine conditions, and typing a metadata key can lose all of it with a single stray click (e.g. clicking just outside the sheet), then has to start the whole setup over with no warning it happened.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Before discarding, compare draft to saved and show a confirmation ('Discard unsaved changes?') when they differ, only closing silently if nothing changed.

evidence.action: Traced closeX's onclick and the backdrop click listener in the source against saveBtn's onclick.
evidence.observed: Both closeX and the backdrop listener call closeOverlay() directly, which only toggles the .open class; only saveBtn's handler ever reads or writes `saved`, so any path other than clicking 'Update' drops the draft with no check or prompt.

critical_high.element: Metadata key field (shown when a refine or scope row's source is 'Payment metadata' / 'Invoice metadata')
critical_high.finding: The metadata key field gives no visual sign that it is required — no asterisk, hint, or inline validation — until after 'Update' is clicked and rejected.
critical_high.user_impact: Users pick a metadata-based source, don't realize a key is mandatory, click Update, get bounced back with an error, and on a first bad experience like this many will abandon the custom-rule setup rather than hunt for what's wrong — matching the known pattern of abandoning multi-field setups when required-ness only surfaces on submit.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Mark the key field as required at all times (e.g. a small 'Required' hint or asterisk next to the label) rather than only after a failed submit.

evidence.action: Per the state map: selected 'Payment metadata' as a refine row's source and left the key empty, then traced applyFieldErrors()/validation() in the source for when the 'Required' error actually appears.
evidence.observed: The '.nl-field-err' text and the key input's invalid styling are only toggled on inside applyFieldErrors(), which is a no-op unless the module-level `submitAttempted` flag is true — and that flag is only set by saveBtn's onclick handler, i.e. after clicking Update.

critical_high.element: 'Configure matching rules →' link, GSP Invoices panel, first toggle row
critical_high.finding: The only entry point into the primary task — setting up the invoice-matching rule — is a small plain-text link tucked under the row's description, visually far less prominent than the blue toggle switch sitting on the same row.
critical_high.user_impact: Users scanning the panel for the control that matters most for their task are drawn to the toggle (which only turns invoice-matching on/off) and can easily miss the link that actually lets them define which invoice a payment matches, especially since it carries no button styling, icon weight, or color distinct from a body-text hyperlink.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Give 'Configure matching rules' the visual weight of a secondary button (border/background) so it reads as the primary way to complete the row's task, not as incidental fine print.

evidence.action: Reviewed the toggle-row markup and computed styles for '.configure-link' versus '.toggle' on the same row.
evidence.observed: '.configure-link' is an unstyled inline text button (background:none, border:0, no padding, plain accent-colored text) placed beneath two lines of paragraph copy, while the toggle switch — which does not open the rule builder — is a full-size colored control on the right with its own visual box.

critical_high.element: GSP settings page — 'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment' toggle (id gspCancel)
critical_high.finding: Toggling this switch produces no visible change anywhere on the settings page at the moment it's flipped; its only effect is a sentence inside the separate matching-rules overlay, which most users won't have open.
critical_high.user_impact: A user deciding this policy (part of setting up how payments apply to invoices) toggles it and sees nothing happen, so they can't tell whether it registered — they are likely to toggle it back and forth, or click the page's Update button unsure of what they are actually saving.
critical_high.suggested_fix: Give the toggle its own on-page state indicator (as the 'Configure matching rules' row already has with its 'Using defaults / Custom rules' badge), or move its plain-language consequence onto the settings page itself instead of only inside the overlay.

evidence.action: Read the gspCancel change handler: it only calls refresh() 'if ($("backdrop").classList.contains("open"))' — i.e. only when the matching-rules overlay happens to already be open — and traced plainEnglish(), the only consumer of gspCancel's value, which renders solely inside the overlay's 'plain terms' rail.
evidence.observed: With the overlay closed (its normal state when a user is on the GSP settings page), flipping gspCancel changes nothing visible on screen; no badge, hint, or text near the toggle updates, unlike the adjacent 'Configure matching rules' control which has a persistent status label.

polish.element: Metadata key field error / submit banner
polish.finding: The metadata-key validation shows the generic 'Required' label and a generic 'Fix the highlighted fields' banner instead of the FDD's specified blocking message.
polish.user_impact: Users get generic validation copy instead of the specific guidance the spec calls for on this exact error.
polish.suggested_fix: Replace the key-field/submit error copy with 'Enter the metadata key to match on.' for this case.

evidence.source: FDD SD-16243 Iteration 1, R10 (specified text: "Enter the metadata key to match on.")

polish.element: Toast — save confirmation on the overlay
polish.finding: The save-success toast reads 'Matching rules updated' without the exclamation mark the canonical Success toast pattern requires for update confirmations.
polish.user_impact: Copy is inconsistent with the product's established success-toast language, which is a stated canonical reference for this UI.
polish.suggested_fix: Change the toast text to 'Matching rules updated!' to match the canonical Success pattern.

polish.element: 'Invoice date is within ⟨days⟩ days' row — enable checkbox in 'Narrow the search'
polish.finding: The date row's own enable checkbox looks identical to every other scope/refine row's checkbox, but for non-admin orgs it is force-checked and disabled with no visible explanation — the reason is only available as a hover tooltip on the checkbox itself.
polish.user_impact: A non-admin user trying to turn off the date limit (a control that behaves exactly like the other scope checkboxes they can freely toggle) will click it, see nothing happen, and have no way to find out why short of hovering precisely over the small checkbox to read a tooltip.
polish.suggested_fix: Replace the silent lock with a visible inline note next to the date row (e.g. 'Ask an admin to change this') instead of relying on a hover-only title attribute.

evidence.action: Traced buildRowEl()'s handling of the date row's enable checkbox when adminEnabled is false.
evidence.observed: For kind === 'date' with adminEnabled false, the code sets enable.checked = true and enable.disabled = true and only communicates why via enable.title = 'Admin-enable the org to turn date limit off' — a native tooltip with no on-screen equivalent.

polish.element: Matching-rules overlay — metadata 'Key' input (shown when source is Payment metadata / Invoice metadata)
polish.finding: The Key field's required status is invisible until the user presses Update: the placeholder just says 'Key' with no required marker, and the 'Required' error only renders after a failed submit attempt.
polish.user_impact: A user filling in a custom rule with a metadata source can complete the rest of the form believing it's ready, click Update, get rejected, and have to notice and fix a field whose necessity was never signaled up front — for anyone who abandons after that first rejection, the rule is never saved.
polish.suggested_fix: Mark the Key field as required at render time (e.g. an asterisk or inline hint) instead of only after a failed submit, so the requirement is visible while the user is still filling in the row.

evidence.action: Reproduced the state map's recon step (select 'Payment metadata' as the source, leave Key empty, click Update) and read the supporting code: submitAttempted is false until saveBtn.onclick sets it true, and applyFieldErrors() — the only place that adds the 'Required' text/invalid state — returns immediately whenever submitAttempted is false.
evidence.observed: Overlay stayed open and a 'Fix the highlighted fields' banner plus a 'Required' message appeared under the Key input only after Update was pressed with the field empty; before that click, the empty Key input carries no required indicator at all.

gaps.text: Focus visibility: the state map records checked/value transitions and reachability for every control but never confirms a visible focus indicator on any of them; whether focus is visibly shown at each step is unverified, not assumed to pass.

Focus return on close: neither the Close (×) pass nor the Escape pass records where focus lands after the overlay closes, so whether focus returns to the 'Configure / Set up matching' trigger is unknown.

Tab order: the map gives a per-zone control inventory and confirms each control is independently reachable, but records no key-by-key Tab traversal, so whether focus moves in the order the screen reads (including into/out of the 'then refine' repeating group) is unconfirmed.

'×' remove-condition button: accessible name is recorded only as '×' with no data on how it's disambiguated when more than one condition row exists; not enough evidence to call this a finding, but it is untested.

Update (primary action) on a valid, error-free save: recon only exercised the blocked path (metadata source with an empty key). Whether a successful save gives visible confirmation a first-timer would notice (the "Matching rules updated" toast) was never recorded, so we can't confirm the save flow actually reassures the user their change stuck.

"Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions" master toggle: recon only recorded turning it off (which disables the Configure link); it was never switched back on with the configurator reopened, so whether a previously saved custom matching rule survives that off/on cycle intact is unknown.

gsp settings switch: with Apply payments off, the entry button becomes unavailable, so the overlay's required 'payments are not being applied' disclosure (R23) was never directly viewed in that state — only inferred from the plain-terms code path.
Plan-gating (below Pro, R22) was never exercised in the state map; the non-configurable state and its plan-requirement messaging could not be checked.

R1 (override/no-fallback), R3 (sort order), R14 (absent vs empty), R15–R17 (outcome/snapshot behaviour) are backend matching-engine semantics not observable from a static UI recon and were not exercised.

Close (×) and Escape-key paths were exercised, but no interaction that reaches a genuinely dirty, then-committed state was recorded, so whether 'Update' actually persists a full custom configuration end-to-end is unconfirmed from the state map alone.

Matching rules overlay: recon recorded the page behind the overlay as not inert while open, but no interaction exercised whether a background control (e.g. gspCancel, gspApply, the Integration select) is actually reachable/operable while the overlay is open, and if so, whether the overlay's own displayed state (badge, plain-terms summary) would go stale or update correctly in that case — commit behaviour for this path is unverified.

Close (×), backdrop click, and Escape were recorded only as 'no discard prompt shown' / 'Escape does not close'; whether the rulesStatus badge or the Configure-matching-rules button transiently show a stale value in the instant after such a discard (versus only after the overlay finishes closing) was not separately exercised.

Close and Update commit paths were marked "not exercised" in this recon's slice of the state map; the behaviors cited above (UX-1 through UX-4) were confirmed by reading the prototype's deterministic JS rather than by a live interaction pass, since the state map didn't record them.

Whether changing the Integration selector (mzkt.by vs another-shop) while the overlay is open actually switches to a separate per-integration matching rule, or only relabels one shared global draft/saved state, was never exercised in recon — source inspection suggests the state is global (not keyed by integration), but this was not confirmed through a live multi-integration interaction, so it is reported here as a gap rather than a finding.

reference_gaps.text: FDD is silent on Escape-key / discard-prompt behaviour for the overlay's close interaction, so the prototype's silent-discard-on-close cannot be scored as a fidelity finding.
R24/Q4 (Generic customer): the FDD marks the required behaviour as an open question, so the prototype's total silence on Generic customer cannot be scored as missing vs. a resolved reference.
Q3 (default finite N, self-serve maximum N, snapshot ceiling) is unresolved in the FDD, so the prototype's 90-day default and 3650-day max cannot be judged against a resolved number.
R27: the FDD explicitly states it does not supply a marketable name, so the prototype's chosen overlay title 'Payment matching rules' cannot be judged against a spec name.
